facts.raw_span: asymptomatic cutaneous lesions on the face that had progressively spread to the trunk and extremities
asthenia and mild intermittent arthralgias
Multiple millimetric erythematous to hyperpigmented monomorphic keratotic papules involving the head, trunk, and extremities
Symmetric annular brown erythematous plaques on the cheeks and temples
No vesicles or pustules
Normal white blood cell count
Mild anemia (hemoglobin level, 11.3 g/dL; normal level 12.50-15.50 g/dL)
Hypocomplementemia
Moderate proteinuria
Raised levels of antinuclear antibodies (>1:160)
Positive: anti-Smith antibodies, SSA/Ro antibodies, SSB/La antibodies, and anti-U1RNP antibodies
Slightly atrophic epidermis with interface dermatitis, individual dyskeratotic keratinocytes, and a superficial perivascular and interstitial infiltrate of neutrophils

concepts.why: The patient's symptoms, including cutaneous lesions, asthenia, and arthralgias, along with laboratory findings of mild anemia, hypocomplementemia, and positive antinuclear antibodies, are consistent with Systemic Lupus Erythematosus.

The patient's cutaneous lesions, including millimetric erythematous to hyperpigmented monomorphic keratotic papules and symmetric annular brown erythematous plaques, are characteristic of Discoid Lupus Erythematosus.

The patient's cutaneous lesions, including millimetric erythematous to hyperpigmented monomorphic keratotic papules and symmetric annular brown erythematous plaques, along with positive antinuclear antibodies, are consistent with Subacute Cutaneous Lupus Erythematosus.

The patient's cutaneous lesions, including millimetric erythematous to hyperpigmented monomorphic keratotic papules, could be consistent with Psoriasis, although the absence of vesicles or pustules and the presence of other symptoms make this diagnosis less likely.
The patient's mild anemia, in the context of chronic disease, is consistent with Anemia of Chronic Disease.
The patient's moderate proteinuria is consistent with Nephrotic Syndrome, although this diagnosis would require further evaluation.
The patient's symptoms, including asthenia, arthralgias, and positive antinuclear antibodies, along with the presence of anti-U1RNP antibodies, are consistent with Mixed Connective Tissue Disease.

The patient's symptoms, including arthralgias, could be consistent with Rheumatoid Arthritis, although the absence of other characteristic symptoms and the presence of other diagnoses make this less likely.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's presentation of asymptomatic cutaneous lesions, asthenia, mild intermittent arthralgias, and specific laboratory findings such as raised levels of antinuclear antibodies and presence of anti-Smith, SSA/Ro, SSB/La, and anti-U1RNP antibodies support Subacute Cutaneous Lupus Erythematosus, which is a subtype of lupus erythematosus that specifically explains the cutaneous manifestations and systemic symptoms without strong contradictions.
